claims.text: The initial non-equilibrium alloy is a metastable, homogeneous, supersaturated solid solution.
Mg is initially uniformly distributed throughout the alloy matrix.
High-temperature exposure promotes diffusion-driven precipitation from the metastable solid solution.
Exposure to a corrosive environment promotes diffusion-driven precipitation from the metastable solid solution.
The precipitated phase is an Mg-rich intermetallic.
During thermal exposure, Mg atoms diffuse and nucleate as a separate intermetallic phase.
Mg-rich precipitates introduce compositional heterogeneity into the matrix.
Precipitation locally modifies high-temperature oxide-scale formation.
Phase separation undermines formation of a uniform protective oxide layer.
The precipitates alter oxide-scale composition or adherence.
The altered oxide scale enhances high-temperature oxidation protection.
Mg-rich precipitates create localized electrochemical differences and galvanic sites.
Galvanic coupling associated with the precipitates increases corrosion rates.
Aged samples will contain detectable Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates and microstructural demarcation relative to the baseline.
Aged samples will exhibit a modified high-temperature oxide scale relative to the baseline.
Aged samples will corrode faster than as-cast or rapidly quenched baseline samples.
The as-cast or rapidly quenched baseline retains a homogeneous metastable solid solution without significant intermetallic precipitation.
The proposed mechanism applies to Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys below 6 g/cm3 when Mg content is sufficient to drive phase separation.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says phase separation undermines a uniform protective oxide layer but also says the resulting scale provides enhanced oxidation protection. These directions are in tension unless a specific compensating effect, such as improved adherence outweighing loss of uniformity, is stated and tested.

The procedure ambiguously treats NaCl exposure as an aging or heat-treatment condition, while the conditions describe elevated-temperature air oxidation and standardized NaCl immersion as separate tests. It is unclear whether precipitation is expected during NaCl immersion, during prior thermal aging, or both.
